provisional_note: Semester 1 (Jul-Dec 2026) follows the official MoEST 2026 calendar. Semester 2 (Jan-May 2027) is inferred from the 2026 pattern and ends before the ACSEE examinations - replace it with the published 2026/2027 almanac before relying on those dates.

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
entries.specific_competence: 1.1. Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles of Chemistry
entries.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concept of chemical equilibria in predicting the direction of reactions for formation of desired products (dynamic equilibrium, ionic equilibrium and acid-base equilibrium)
teaching_learning_activities: Group discussion: Guide students to discuss the concept of chemical equilibria
entries.assessment: The concept of chemical equilibria are clearly described
resources: Ethanol, ethanoic acid, source of heat,
NH3, H2SO4, water, wood ash, lemons, acid,  bases, weak and strong acids
weak and strong bases, pH meter,
BaSO4, CaCO3, AgCl, AgNO3, Na2SO4, and Ba(NO3)2
entries.references: TIE, Chemistry for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Six: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
entries.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements according to their position in the periodic table
entries.learning_activity: (a) Describe the physical and chemical properties of transition elements (variable oxidation states, catalytic properties, magnetic properties, alloy formation)
teaching_learning_activities: Interactive simulation: Employ visual aids to guide students to describe physical and chemical properties of transition elements
entries.assessment: Physical and chemical properties of transition elements are clearly described
resources: Wall charts of modern periodic table, wall charts showing variable oxidation states of first row transition elements (atomic numbers 21– 30),
wall chart showing  diagrams of split d-orbital,
finely divided first row transition elements and their chlorides, carbonates, sulphates, hydroxides and nitrates,
entries.references: TIE, Chemistry for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Six: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

teaching_learning_activities: Practical: Guide students to perform experiments of the selected Chemistry themes started in    Form Five
Project: Guide students to  analyse the experimental data by using ICT facilities and submit the  synthesised product(s) and scientific report for assessment
entries.assessment: Scientific report of the project is clearly written and quality project product(s) are obtained
resources: sample of project reports and chemistry based software
